> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 60b42cd0b79d99252a003b5374b604e36157de79` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7d3af2df0ca548a596f44aedf49856958be6468d` — the merge of head `bc359a7c731f390b322a3958ffd0d2a259308dec` into base `60b42cd0b79d99252a003b5374b604e36157de79`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7d3af2df0ca548a596f44aedf49856958be6468d && git checkout 7d3af2df0ca548a596f44aedf49856958be6468d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 60b42cd0b79d99252a003b5374b604e36157de79 bc359a7c731f390b322a3958ffd0d2a259308dec && git checkout -B drift-repro 60b42cd0b79d99252a003b5374b604e36157de79 && git merge --no-ff bc359a7c731f390b322a3958ffd0d2a259308dec

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 60b42cd0b79d99252a003b5374b604e36157de79
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 60b42cd0b79d99252a003b5374b604e36157de79` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Nothing was built, no test was run, nothing was posted. The one script run was the read-only `check-governed-merges.mjs --branch`.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. Parity with the resolver — yes, in every composition.**

The resolver's predicate (`resolve-authz-context.ts:943-949`): `false` when walled, `false` when no Default Organization is nameable, else `grantOrganizationOf(grant) === anchor.defaultOrganizationId`, where `grantOrganizationOf` (`:921-928`) answers `null` for a NULL, absent or blank `organization_id`/`organizationId`. The guard's `anchorOwnerTest` at the head (`last-admin-guard.ts:1054-1066`): `defaultOrganizationId` is read only when `!postureEnforcesWall(resolveTenancyPosture())` and some link names an owner (`:1060-1062`), and the returned test is `owner !== undefined && owner === defaultOrganizationId` (`:1065`) with `ownerOf = toId(link.organization_id ?? link.organizationId)` (`:1059`) and `toId` (`:603-607`) answering `undefined` for a non-string, an empty string, `null` or absent. Composition by composition:

- Walled vs `single`: walled makes `defaultOrganizationId` undefined, so nothing anchors (`:1060`, matching `:943-947`). Under `single` the Default Organization's grant anchors, and only it. The count site additionally gates the whole grant leg on `!postureEnforcesWall` (`:1124-1127`), as the resolver gates `anchorReadsDefaultOrganization` on `!walled` (`:1622-1624`).
- No nameable Default Organization (zero, or several with none `default`): the guard's `readDefaultOrganizationId` (`:1009-1039`) answers `undefined` (slug `default`, else the only one, `:1029-1039`); the resolver's (`:963-971`) is the same definition. Nothing anchors on either side.
- No `sys_organization` registered: the guard returns `undefined` from the registry probe (`:1013-1016`); the resolver's `registryHoldsObject` (`:1233-1241`) does the same. Nothing anchors on either side, so a lean embedding has no grant-anchored administrator, exactly as the resolver reads it.
- NULL, absent or blank owner: `toId` yields `undefined`; the predicate's left conjunct fails (`:1065`). The resolver's `grantOrganizationOf` yields `null`, never equal to a string id. Agreed.
- Someone the guard counts and the resolver does not, or the reverse: none found. The config anchor `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` is counted by the guard under every posture through the resolver's own `matchesConfiguredPlatformAdmin` (`:1227-1245`, predicate at `:1240`), and the resolver confers it under every posture (`:1794-1796`). Organization owners and admins (`:1178-1190`) are the guard's grade 2 by design, not a platform-admin claim; unchanged. The set-defined and switched-off gates (`:1125-1127`) mirror the resolver's catalog and ledger reads; unchanged.
- Every count site uses the one predicate: `resolveAdminUserIds` (`:1134-1138`, consumed at `:1158`), the switched-off evidence (`:1321-1322`), the dangling evidence (`:1353`, consumed at `:1367`), and `enforceStanding` (`:1565-1640`) and `judgeOrganizationDelete` (`:1886-1896`) only ever call `resolveAdminUserIds`, so they inherit it. No second spelling remains: `grep` for `unscoped`, `or by none`, `PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL_ENV` and `walledRemedy` over both source files returns nothing.

**2. The failure direction — the fail-open is closed; no legitimate fail-closed is opened.**

- Closed: with a verified `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` account beside an organization-less holder, the holder is no longer a survivor, so banning the owner is refused. Pinned on a lean embedding and on a pre-18 store (`last-admin-guard.anchor-parity.test.ts`, the two negative pins, approx `:243-283`) and on `single` in the config-anchor suite (`last-admin-guard.config-anchor.test.ts`, "REFUSES it under `single` too when the surviving grant is organization-less").
- A fresh `single` install: the boot invariant creates the Default Organization before any user, the promotion writes the grant owned by it, `links.some(ownerOf)` is true, the slug read finds it, the holder counts (`:1060-1065`, `:1029-1031`). The positive control pins it (anchor-parity, approx `:286-311`) and the unchanged `last-admin-guard.default-organization.test.ts` still pins the served shape. R1 in the dev report observed it on a real boot.
- A walled install with the organizations runtime and a declared owner: no grant counted before this PR either (`:1124`); the owner counts through the config anchor. The wall arm of the L5 suite pins the refusal for both owners (`default-organization` and `none`) under `group` and `isolated`.
- An 18.0.0-born store: its one `admin_full_access` grant is owned by the Default Organization (measurement, fixture `database.sql:684`), so it counts.
- Refusal texts: both emptied-not-fresh refusals (`:1329-1340`, `:1379-1390`) now say "in-window Default Organization grant(s)" and keep the remedies "switch the set back on" and "restore the set". Both are reachable only under `single` with Default-Organization-owned grants, where restoring the set or its activation does restore standing, so each named remedy is true. Under a wall `anchorOwnerTest` admits nothing, so `stranded` and `dangling` are empty and neither refusal fires; the retired walled-remedy clause and the `PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL_ENV` import (`:326`) were therefore unreachable text, and the docblock at `:1300-1304` says so. The one trade: a dangling or switched-off organization-less grant is no longer "emptied" evidence in any posture (`:1353`, `:1321`), so a write in that state is read as the bootstrap window; the resolver recognises nobody from that row, so nobody's standing is at stake. Pinned in the config-anchor suite ("a switched-off set is emptied-not-fresh evidence only through a grant that anchors", arms `isolated/default-organization`, `isolated/none`, `single/none`, with the `single/default-organization` control still refusing).

**3. The bootstrap — the right admin is still found and bound.**

`ensure-default-organization.ts:503-516`: `findDefaultOrganizationId` (`:342-347`, slug `default` else the sole organization, through `tryFind`) then one read of `sys_user_permission_set` with `organization_id: defaultOrgId`, or none. The config anchor is read first (`:447`, `:288-307`), unchanged. The grant leg is skipped under a wall (`:469-470`), unchanged.
- Walled fresh boot: the grant leg is not reached; the verified declared owner is found through the config anchor and bound; the Default Organization is created or re-used by slug (`:555-559`). R4 in the dev report observed it.
- `single` fresh boot: the Default Organization exists before any user (the boot invariant), the promotion's grant is owned by it, the trigger on the grant insert (`:267-271`) runs this helper, the Default-Organization read finds the oldest grant, and its holder is promoted from the reconciler's `member` row to `owner`. R1 observed it.
- No path creates no admin where one should be bound: under `single` the engine derives the owner only when exactly one organization exists and refuses at zero or several (ADR-0131 D9), so a grant cannot precede the organization, and with several organizations and none `default` the resolver anchors nothing either, so `no_admin` is the agreeing answer. No path binds the wrong one: another organization's grant is not read; an organization-less holder is never bound (the new pin at `ensure-default-organization.test.ts:216-232` asserts the read's `where` names only the Default Organization; the pin at `:234-247` asserts no grant read at all).

**4. The tests — none weakened; the parity suite is real.**

`it(` counts before/after: last-admin-guard 110/110; config-anchor 18/19; re-pricing 9/9; activation-ledger 9/9; scim 13/13; ensure-default-organization 42/44; default-org-bootstrap-once 5/5; auth-plugin 100/100; anchor-parity 0/4 `it(` blocks (one a 10-row loop: 13 cases). No `skip`, `todo` or `only` anywhere in the nine files. Total new cases 16 = 3448 - 3432, matching the PR body.
Spot-checked (27): the #5892 and #5941 "platform admin counts, a SCOPED grant does not" pair; #5978 path 1 (grant survivor) and path 3 (re-scoping the Default Organization's grant refused, row stays `DEFAULT_ORG`); #6084 and #8613 evidence pins; config-anchor L2 and the FIFTH-shape "ALLOWS" case (grants now owned by `DEFAULT_ORG`); the whole L5 block (the walled refusal over 2 postures x 2 owners, the new `single`/organization-less refusal, the `single`/Default-Organization control, "stops refusing WRONGLY" over 3 arms, the `single` revocation control, the evidence arms and their control); re-pricing "deleting the LAST grant row is permitted"; activation-ledger `seedGrantAdmin`; scim `makePlatformAdmin` (now through the engine, owned by `DEFAULT_ORG`); ensure-default-organization "creates and binds" (moved to a config-only rig), the OLDEST-grant case, the walled L5 case (asserts no insert against the seeded Default Organization), and the two new pins; default-org-bootstrap-once's rig; auth-plugin's two org-create cases (now through a verified declared owner, with a lazily-owned `promotionGrant` getter at `:11-33`); the parity matrix, both negative pins and the positive control.
- Purpose changes are all stated: the old "names the remedy that WORKS under a wall" case became the evidence pin because the clause it asserted no longer exists (in-file comment); the auth-plugin org-create cases go through the config anchor because a grant cannot anchor before the organization exists (in-file comment and PR body).
- Pre-18 rows assert the NEW direction: config-anchor `legacyStore` cases seed beneath the engine and assert refusal of the owner's write (single/none) and permit of the inert row's revocation; the bootstrap pins assert `no_admin`; the parity negative pins assert `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403 and `banned` falsy.
- `relaxEveryRegisteredTenantColumn` is dropped from last-admin-guard, re-pricing, activation-ledger and scim (each now registers `sys_organization`, writes a `default` row at boot and owns grants by it; the pool's `keepBootOrganizations` keeps the row and refuses a case that changed it, `sqlite-engine-pool.testkit.ts:60-66`, `:139-143`, `:160-167`). It stays in config-anchor behind `legacyStore` and in anchor-parity behind `nullableTenantColumn`, both only for cases that model a pre-18 row. Justified.
- `last-admin-guard.anchor-parity.test.ts` is real: a fresh `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver` better-sqlite3 `:memory:`, `engine.syncSchemas()`, the real `bindTestSecurityCatalog`, the real `registerLastAdminGuard`, and the real `resolveAuthzContext` from `@objectstack/core` with an injected `getSession` (the resolver reads it at `resolve-authz-context.ts:551-555`). The matrix asserts the engine's own verdict on the write (D9 code, `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_NOTNULL`, derived owner, or stored null) and then that the guard refuses the ban exactly when the resolver grades the holder. Discrimination: with `owner === undefined ||` restored, the `nullable / no-object / single / stored-null` row would read the holder as counted (ban refused, expected permitted) and both negative pins would admit the owner's ban; the positive control stays green under both and guards the other direction. So the stated ablation turns them red.
- driver-memory to sqlite: acceptable. The guard has no driver branch; the row reaches the table through the engine's no-organization-object exit on both drivers and only the column could refuse it; the measurement already recorded driver-memory's own fail-open, and `check:driver-memory-census` refuses a new consumer without a ruling. The nullable sqlite column reproduces the same guard path.

**6. Docs.** `authorization.mdx:136-142`: "a grant owned by the Default Organization is sufficient only under `single`; a grant owned by no organization anchors nothing in any posture, and under the walled postures no grant is an anchor" matches `resolve-authz-context.ts:943-949`. `:364-365` and `:453-454` drop "unscoped" correctly. The new paragraph `:484-491` states the guard's three grades and the lean-embedding consequence accurately against `last-admin-guard.ts:131-157`.

**7. #25016.** `auth-manager.ts:8163-8190`: for the Default Organization the standing judge is asked first (`:8175-8183`, a `PERMISSION_DENIED` is re-thrown as `FORBIDDEN` 403) and the record count second (`:8185-8190`, `CONFLICT` 409). This PR touches neither; the judge (`last-admin-guard.ts:1886-1896`) runs the same `enforceStanding` with the members as a companion delete, and with a pending Default-Organization delete `readDefaultOrganizationId` (`:1018-1039`) re-derives the anchor after the write. The only verdict that moves is the one the fix exists for: an organization-less holder no longer counts as the survivor that admitted deleting the organization whose owner is the last administrator. The Default-Organization delete pins in the unchanged `last-admin-guard.default-organization.test.ts` keep their contract, and the dev report re-ran the #25016 pins (21/21) and the full dogfood battery on this head.

### ② Semver level

`patch` is right. `Metadata-protocol: none` (no metadata key, value or type changes; the rows read differently are stored grant rows, not authorable metadata), and under AGENTS.md item 3 the level follows the kind alone: `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is correct: `registerLastAdminGuard` refuses a write it used to permit. Both declaration lines are line-initial in the changeset (`:7-8`) and in the PR body, and `clause2-line.mjs` reads exactly that shape; both `Check Changeset` runs on the head are green. Present: the BREAKING banner (`:12`), FROM and TO for `registerLastAdminGuard` (`:14`), the two verdict directions (`:15-16`), the walled-evidence note (`:17`), `ensureDefaultOrganization`'s FROM and TO (`:18`), who sees it (`:20`), the embedder's remedy naming `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` plus an owner or admin `sys_member` row, or registering `sys_organization`, plus `os migrate organization-ownership` for a pre-18 database (`:22`), and exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker (`:10`) in the same form as the 7a-2 changeset. Every sentence checked against the head is true. The public export's behaviour change is described in both directions and in the evidence predicate; see B1 for one sentence that is true but narrower than the change.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **B1 — not blocking.** Changeset `:17` scopes the emptied-evidence change to "Under a walled posture", but the same verdict change holds under `single` for an organization-less stranded or dangling grant (`last-admin-guard.ts:1321`, `:1353`; pinned by the `single/none` arm in the config-anchor evidence case). The sentence is true, and the `single` direction is covered by `:16` ("permits ... deleting or revoking an organization-less holder"), so nothing is misdescribed; a follow-up could say "in any posture".
- **B2 — not blocking.** `last-admin-guard.anchor-parity.test.ts` `resolverStanding` reads `ctx.positions.includes('platform_admin')`, the wide list the resolver tells readers not to use for standing (`resolve-authz-context.ts:1897-1901`); `ResolvedAuthzContext.posture` is the rung. In this fixture no `sys_user_position` row exists, so the two readings coincide and the pin discriminates; a later fixture with a position spelled `platform_admin` would blur it. Suggest `ctx.posture === 'PLATFORM_ADMIN'`.
- **B3 — not blocking.** PR body "0 of 16 paths" is stale from the removed driver-memory devDependency commit; the final list is 14 and my run reads "0 of 14" (NOT governed). The `dependencies` label is likewise stale. PR-body and label only; the changeset is unaffected.
- **B4 — not blocking.** The PR is still a draft (`mergeable_state: blocked`); it needs un-drafting and this record before the queue.
- **B5 — observation, pre-existing, not this PR's.** The guard's `readDefaultOrganizationId` (`:1013-1016`) treats an engine with no `registry.getObject` as holding the organization object and scans the table (fail-closed on a missing table); the resolver's `registryHoldsObject` (`:1233-1241`) answers true there too. Both fail safe; parity is unaffected.
- **CI (item 8):** red required checks: none. Pending required checks: none. All five required contexts on `980cdc13ce` are `success`: `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Every other run is `success` or `skipped` (opt-in and schedule-only jobs); both `Check Changeset` runs and `Dogfood Regression Gate` are `success`; no run is in progress.

## Seat check

- **Shape.** 15 paths, +897 / -322. `check-governed-merges`: NOT governed, under 3,000 lines. This is an ordinary queue landing.
- **What it does.**
  - The last-admin guard's `anchorOwnerTest` counts only the Default Organization's `admin_full_access` grant, so it answers the resolver's `grantAnchorsPlatformStanding` question (7a-2) in every composition.
